claim: After refinement, the evaluation set is high quality for judging prompt-fixable Account Security Alert tutor prompt behavior before live Promptfoo runs.

criteria.text: Coverage of prompt-fixable feedback requirements by cases/rubrics, excluding non-prompt issues like latency and real multi-bot UI.

evidence.text: Break the question-every-turn pattern.
The tutor must break the question-every-turn pattern.
Add genuine disagreement and correction.
When the student is wrong or incomplete, the tutor must correct the mistake directly instead of validating unsafe reasoning.
Stabilize the persona. Pick one consistent voice
The tutor should keep one consistent knowledgeable-peer voice
Reduce boilerplate encouragement.
The tutor should reduce hollow encouragement.
Real-world tools (URL decompilers, reverse image search, HTTPS indicators)
URL expander/checker, reverse image search, HTTPS/domain distinction.
Use third-person testimonials, not first-person AI claims.
third-person testimonials or general examples, not first-person AI claims.
Simplify language for younger audiences.
language that works for younger or confused students
This evaluates prompt behavior only. It does not call Supabase, does not exercise the React app, and does not verify UI latency.

criteria.reasoning: I accept audit2 iteration 1 on c1 under the refined claim: the prompt-fixable feedback items have explicit rubrics and case coverage, while latency and real multi-bot UI are excluded by scope.

counterevidence.text: Fix response latency. Add a typing indicator.

criteria.text: Rubric observability and pass/fail clarity including per-case assertion alignment.

criteria.reasoning: I partly accept the refinement because direct few-shot duplicates were moved to neighboring scams, but the remaining suite is still a single visible scenario with cases that closely target exact candidate-prompt facts and checks. That is useful smoke coverage, not strong overfitting control for a high-quality pre-live judge.

counterevidence.text: Style examples from neighboring scam situations. These examples show the desired behavior pattern but intentionally do not answer the evaluation cases directly:
It requires the improved prompt to pass at least 80% for each metric and to match or beat the current prompt on every metric.

open_questions: Should c5 require at least one held-out or neighboring-scenario case before live Promptfoo runs, or is exact Account Security Alert smoke coverage sufficient for this stage?
disputed_points_if_any: c1: audit1/audit3 iteration 1 failed partly because latency and multi-bot feedback were treated as uncovered; I now pass c1 because the iteration 2 claim explicitly excludes non-prompt issues.
c3: all iteration 1 reviewers failed because all seven rubrics were global; I now pass c3 because assertions are per-case and aligned with applicable_requirements.
c5: all iteration 1 reviewers failed from candidate-prompt/eval overlap; I still fail c5 because direct few-shot leakage improved but exact scenario fact overlap and no held-out expansion remain.
